atoms.obligation: Work through the review's sections in the given order, completing each before starting the next.
atoms.lesson: This skill guides the platform engineer through a cost review end to end. Work the sections in order; each one names an obligation you can be held to. The sections are, in order: (1) cost reduction search order, (2) dependencies, (3) staged rollout with a kill switch, (4) cost and compute, (5) measure the current state, (6) close against a definition of done, (7) communication and stakeholders.

atoms.obligation: Attack the cheapest reductions first and optimise the implementation only after the easy savings are exhausted.
atoms.lesson:
The platform engineer owns this step.

Work the list in order of effort-to-saving: delete what nobody reads, apply lifecycle rules to cold storage, stop recomputing what has not changed, right-size the instances, and only then optimise the code.

atoms.obligation: Attribute current spend to each workload before you start deciding what to change.
atoms.lesson: Attribute cost per pipeline before you start, because the intuition about which job is expensive is wrong more often than it is right. The platform engineer owns this step.

atoms.obligation: Enumerate every upstream input and downstream consumer, including undocumented ones, before changing anything.
atoms.lesson:
The platform engineer owns this step.

Enumerate upstream feeds and downstream consumers, including unofficial ones — read the access logs, not the docs — and record how and how fast each consumer would detect a failure.

atoms.obligation: Write down the outcome of each completed step in the shared written record for this work.
atoms.lesson: "Record the outcome of this step in the cost review notes." The instruction is repeated verbatim at the end of three sections: 2. Dependencies: what is required; 3. Roll out in stages with a kill switch — non-negotiable; and 5. Measure the current state before changing it. The destination is the cost review notes.

atoms.obligation: Promote the change through environments in sequence, giving each stage a pass criterion and a soak period.
atoms.lesson:
This section applies to every cost review without exception.

Move through the environments in order and give each stage a pass criterion and a soak period.
atoms.anchor: 3. Roll out in stages with a kill switch — non-negotiable

atoms.obligation: Put the change behind a switch that disables it without a redeploy, and test that switch first.
atoms.lesson: Put the change behind a flag that can be flipped off without a deploy, and confirm the flip works before the first real traffic reaches it. This section applies to every cost review without exception.
atoms.anchor: 3. Roll out in stages with a kill switch — non-negotiable

atoms.obligation: Estimate the cost of any large run before you launch it.
atoms.lesson: Estimate cost before launching anything large: scenes x cost-per-scene for compute, bytes x rate x months for storage, plus egress. A run that finishes and blows the quarter's budget is a failed run.

atoms.obligation: Compare the estimate against the budget and obtain sign-off once it passes the agreed threshold.
atoms.lesson: Compare against the budget line and get sign-off past the agreed threshold. A run that finishes and blows the quarter's budget is a failed run.

atoms.obligation: Capture a baseline measurement under matched conditions before you change anything.
atoms.lesson:
Apply this before the cost review leaves your hands.

Record the baseline under matched conditions before changing anything; otherwise the after-number means nothing.
atoms.anchor: 5. Measure the current state before changing it

atoms.obligation: Define completion up front as a list of statements that someone else can verify.
atoms.lesson: Define done up front as a list of verifiable statements. Retro-fitted criteria and uncheckable criteria both invalidate the closure. This section applies to every cost review without exception.
atoms.anchor: 6. Close against an explicit definition of done for this cost review

atoms.obligation: Close the work only by walking the completion list and attaching evidence for every item.
atoms.lesson: To close, walk the list and attach evidence per item. Retro-fitted criteria and uncheckable criteria both invalidate the closure.
atoms.anchor: 6. Close against an explicit definition of done for this cost review

atoms.obligation: Stop and escalate rather than proceeding when you cannot satisfy this requirement.
atoms.lesson: If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate. This applies to closing against an explicit definition of done, which applies to every cost review without exception.
atoms.anchor: 6. Close against an explicit definition of done for this cost review

atoms.obligation: Lead with who is affected and what they should do, keeping technical detail short and below that.
atoms.lesson: Open with impact, not mechanism: who is affected, over what period, and what they should do. Keep the technical explanation below that, in one short paragraph.

atoms.obligation: Give a time for the next update whenever the situation is still moving.
atoms.lesson: Give a next-update time whenever the situation is still moving.

atoms.obligation: Tell affected people about a problem before they can discover it through their own monitoring.
atoms.lesson: Never let a stakeholder learn about a problem from their own dashboard first.

atoms.obligation: Before finishing, check off every required step of the process against the closing list.
atoms.lesson:
- [ ] Cost reduction search order
- [ ] Map upstream and downstream dependencies
- [ ] Roll out in stages with a kill switch
- [ ] Estimate compute and storage cost before running
- [ ] Measure the current state before changing it
- [ ] Close against an explicit definition of done
- [ ] Communicate to stakeholders in their terms
